steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated (atopic dermatitis lesional) and control skin, and in which direction?

grounding.reason: Two-group unpaired design, 6 vs 6, raw gene counts: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage per R-0001@9a17; Salmon counts with no length input fitted without offset and the loss reported per R-0169@18ab

constraints: filter_low_counts: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least the smallest group size (6) of samples (doi:10.12688/f1000research.7035.1, doi:10.1073/pnas.0914005107); do not over-filter — independent filtering later does the rest.
normalize: median-of-ratios size factors inside the model; do not pre-scale, transform, or pre-normalize the counts (doi:10.1186/s13059-014-0550-8).

model_design: import = gene_counts_without_length_offset (doi:10.12688/f1000research.7563.2). The missing_input for a length correction is per-sample quantification directories (quant.sf / abundance.h5 / genes.results) or a per-gene-per-sample average transcript length table; neither was delivered. model_design: set the condition reference level explicitly (control as reference); name the contrast as factor/numerator/denominator so positive log2FC means higher in treated (vignette:DESeq2/1.52.0#note-on-factor-levels).
differential_expression: Wald test; keep Cook's-distance outlier flagging on (count_outlier_policy = flag_and_report_na) (doi:10.1186/s13059-014-0550-8).
shrink_lfc: apeglm for the reported fold change; keep the unshrunken estimate and its SE beside it; keep p-values from the unshrunken fit (doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/bty895).

multiple_testing: BH at alpha 0.05, independent filtering on, p-value histogram inspected before trusting adjusted values; never filter or select by unadjusted p-value or by fold change alone (doi:10.1073/pnas.0914005107, doi:10.1111/j.2517-6161.1995.tb02031.x).

plan.title: AD lesional vs control differential expression
plan.analytical_narrative: The question is a two-group differential expression call on skin: 6 treated (atopic dermatitis lesional) vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, one gene-level Salmon count table (12,000 genes x 12 samples) whose length-correction state is unknown because the per-sample quant.sf files were not delivered. The plan follows the grounded procedure for this exact situation. T1S1 runs sample-structure QC first (blind VST, PCA on the 500 top-variance genes, sample-distance heatmap) so any outlier or condition-independent structure is seen before testing. T1S2 fits DESeq2 on the counts as delivered — median-of-ratios size factors, no length offset — with a minimal 10-counts-in-6-samples pre-filter, Wald test on the explicit treated-vs-control contrast, apeglm-shrunken fold changes for ranking and reporting, BH at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering, and separate reporting of Cook's-distance outlier NAs and the p-value histogram. Because the counts came from a transcript quantifier with no length input, the model omits the length offset and the report must state that isoform-use changes can surface as gene-level DE (R-0169@18ab) — tximport cannot be used and no length input is invented. T1S4 runs edgeR quasi-likelihood (TMM, robust dispersion) as the second method: at 6 vs 6, near the low end of the replicate range, the DESeq2/edgeR overlap defines the high-confidence DE set (R-0042@54e1). T1S3 consolidates everything into one report with fit diagnostics, the method-overlap table, both shrunken and unshrunken effect sizes, and a reproducibility record. No enrichment or pathway step is included because the research question asks only which genes are differentially expressed.

grounding.reason: Two-group unpaired design, 6 vs 6, raw gene counts: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage per R-0001@9a17; Salmon counts with no length input fitted without offset and the loss reported per R-0169@18ab

steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test, treated vs control, with apeglm shrinkage
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated (atopic dermatitis lesional) and control skin, and in which direction?

acceptance_criteria: edgeR DE gene table with logFC, logCPM, F, FDR, keyed by the same gene identifiers as T1S2.
TMM normalization factors and filterByExpr retention counts reported.
n_de at FDR < 0.05 for treated vs control reported on the edgeR side.
Tables are joinable to the DESeq2 results by gene identifier with no silent identifier mismatches (mismatches counted and reported).
caveats: The two tools agree on most genes at this replicate number but each calls some genes the other does not; the disagreement grows at low counts. The intersection is the high-confidence set, not the union.

edgeR applies TMM normalization, which unlike DESeq2's median-of-ratios does not need the length correction to agree between methods — both correct for library composition, so the comparison is valid on the same counts.
constraints: Normalization: TMM scaling factors; do not pre-normalize the counts (edgeR counterpart of doi:10.1186/s13059-014-0550-8).
Filter: filterByExpr before the model takes the place of DESeq2's independent filtering.
Test: glmQLFit with robust dispersion, glmQLFTest on the treated-vs-control contrast; select genes at FDR < 0.05.
Use the same pre-filter spirit as T1S2 (low-count genes removed) so the two gene sets are comparable.
steps.description: Independent second method on the same filtered counts: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test (TMM normalization, robust dispersion) on treated vs control, to report the overlap with the DESeq2 Wald results per the robustness rule (R-0042@54e1). edgeR is the named alternative method (M-0003) for this design; at 6 vs 6 its agreement with DESeq2 defines the high-confidence gene set.

grounding.reason: edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test is the permitted alternative (M-0003) to DESeq2 Wald per R-0001@9a17; run both and report the overlap per R-0042@54e1 at the low end of the replicate range

steps.name: edgeR quasi-likelihood robustness check
steps.question: Do the DE calls from a second count model (edgeR QL F-test) agree with the DESeq2 Wald calls for treated vs control?

acceptance_criteria: Method, package versions, design formula, named contrast (treated vs control, reference = control), thresholds, n_tested, and n_de stated before the gene tables (doi:10.1093/bib/bbz124).

Explicit statement of the Salmon import limitation: length correction state unknown, no length offset applied, and a change in isoform use can therefore appear as differential expression (doi:10.12688/f1000research.7563.2).
MA plot and dispersion plot placed before the gene tables, each with one line on what it shows.
P-value histogram reported with its shape beside the significance counts.
Gene table columns: unshrunken log2FoldChange, shrunken log2FoldChange (estimator named), lfcSE, statistic, p-value, padj; genes ranked by shrunken log2FoldChange; selection by padj < 0.05.

Robustness table: n_de from DESeq2, n_de from edgeR QL, intersection size; the intersection labeled the high-confidence set and single-method genes listed as method-attributed secondary sets (doi:10.1261/rna.053959.115).
Counts of NA p-values attributed to each cause (Cook's outlier flag vs independent filter).
Reproducibility record stored with the results: session info, seed, package versions, gene identifier space (doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285).
caveats: The report must not overstate: with 6 vs 6 and an unknown Salmon length-correction state, the DE list is a solid but not definitive answer to the research question — state both limitations in plain language.
Do not present the union of the two methods as the result.
constraints: report: effect_columns = log2FoldChange, shrunken_log2FoldChange, lfcSE; rank by the shrunken value; keep test p-values from the unshrunken fit (doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/bty895).
report: fit_diagnostics = ma_plot, dispersion_plot (vignette:DESeq2/1.52.0#ma-plot).
report: robustness = overlap_of_two_methods — intersection is the high-confidence set, single-method genes listed as secondary (doi:10.1261/rna.053959.115).
report: report_fields = method, versions, design, thresholds, n_tested, n_de, session_info (doi:10.1093/bib/bbz124).
report: reproducibility_record = session_info, seed, package_versions, collection_version, annotation_release (doi:10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003285).
The report must carry the R-0169@18ab caveat about the missing length input verbatim in substance: state that the length offset is lost and that isoform-use changes can surface as gene-level DE.
steps.description: Consolidated report of the treated-vs-control DE analysis: method/versions/design/thresholds header, MA and dispersion diagnostics, p-value histogram, DESeq2 vs edgeR overlap table (intersection as the high-confidence set), full ranked gene table with both unshrunken and apeglm-shrunken log2FC, and the reproducibility record — including the explicit statement that the Salmon length offset is unknown and absent from the model.
steps.name: Report: DE gene tables, diagnostics, method overlap
steps.question: What is the final, reproducible answer to which genes differ between treated (atopic dermatitis lesional) and control skin, with the reliability of that answer stated?

plan.title: AD lesional vs control differential expression

flags.message: A quantifier name alone does not establish that the length correction occurred. If the counts come from Salmon, kallisto, or RSEM as a gene-level table, with no per-sample quantification files and no average transcript length table, the import state is not established. Ask for the per-sample quantification files, quant.sf, abundance.h5, or genes.results, or for the average transcript length table per gene and sample. If neither arrives, fit the count model on the counts as delivered, with no length offset, and state in the plan and in the report that the length offset is lost and that a change in isoform use can show as differential expression. Do not run tximport on a gene table, because tximport imports transcript estimates, and do not invent a length input.
